title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, and Evidence Workflows
author: Ava Chen
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineering, SRE, product security, and compliance teams to implement and validate controls for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-managed services (hosted API, control plane, telemetry ingestion) and guidance for Dedicated and Private deployments where applicable.
- Parties: security (owner), eng-sre, eng-infra, eng-platform, product, and customer-success for customer-facing controls.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Goal: Ensure least-privilege access across control planes, internal tools, and customer-facing admin UIs.

Roles and role mapping:
- System roles (examples): security-admin, infra-admin, runtime-operator, sde, readonly, support-agent.
- Principle: role names are coarse-grained; access to resources is controlled through resource-level grants (projects, customer-ids, clusters).

Authentication requirements:
- Primary auth provider: SSO via Okta (OIDC).
- M2M services: service accounts with short-lived tokens (default 1h) issued by our token service (token-service.redwood-internal).
- MFA: enforced for all human users with roles security-admin, infra-admin, and anyone with access to PII or customer secrets.

RBAC policies and enforcement:
- Policy store: central ABAC/RBAC engine (authz.redwood) using XACML-like policies and attribute-based conditions (user.role, user.team, resource.env).
- Enforcement points: API gateway (edge-auth), control-plane service (controlplane-authz), internal admin UI (ui-authz).
- Policy review cadence: quarterly; emergency changes must follow change-management templates and be recorded in the audit log.

Onboarding/offboarding:
1. New hire AAD/Okta account requested via People Ops.
2. Security reviewer approves role assignment for prod access.
3. Access revoked within 2 hours of offboarding ticket.

SLOs and thresholds:
- 100% of prod admin access changes logged within 30s.
- Offboarding actions completed within 2 hours for high-privilege roles.

Ownership: security (policy), eng-infra (SSO integration), eng-platform (enforcement).

2) Audit Logging

Goal: Provide tamper-evident, searchable audit trails for authentication, authorization decisions, admin actions, deployment changes, and data exports.

Log types and retention:
- Auth logs: login, SSO assertion, token issuance — retention 1 year (hosted), configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- Admin actions: role changes, billing exports, canary rollouts — retention 3 years for enterprise customers (as contractual).
- Data access logs: queries to customer data stores, model artifacts downloads — retention 3 years for regulated customers.

Implementation details:
- Ingestion pipeline: logs -> Fluent-bit -> secure Kafka topic (audit-events) -> WORM S3 (encrypted, immutability tag) + Splunk/Elastic cluster for analysis.
- Integrity: daily signed manifests and SHA256 of daily log segments stored in a dedicated evidence bucket (evidence.redwood/internal-audit).
- Alerting: anomalous admin activity (roles changed outside working hours, sudden export > 1GB) triggers a P1 security alert to PagerDuty.

Access controls to audit data:
- Read access only via privileged analytics role with MFA and explicit justification in ticketing system.
- Audit logs are not editable; any corrections must be recorded as new audit entries.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency controls:
- Default: customer data resides in the region selected at provisioning (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Cross-region replication disabled unless explicitly requested and approved by customer and security.
- For Private deployments, we provide a residency checklist and validation script (residency-checker.sh) to verify network routes and storage endpoints.

Retention policy (hosted):
- Inference metadata and logs: 365 days.
- Short-term caches (KV cache): 7 days or configurable per-customer.
- Customer-provided data (files/gen-uploads): retention per contract; default 90 days.

Data deletion and export:
- Export process: Authenticated request -> data-export-service (async) -> customer-signed S3 URL. Exports are logged in audit with pre-signed URL expiry limited to 24 hours.
- Deletion: issued via API or console; deletion workflow triggers asynchronous purge and records tombstone in audit logs; full physical deletion (S3 lifecycle + overwrite) completes within 30 days unless legal hold is present.

4) Secure SDLC

Standards and gates:
- Mandatory code review for all code touching production infra or customer data.
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST) on every PR for supported languages; SCA for dependencies.
- Container image scanning (CVE) in build pipeline; images with critical CVEs blocked from deployment.
- Secrets scanning: pre-commit checks and pipeline-stage secrets-detection.

Build & deploy controls:
- Artifacts (images, packages) are signed by CI and stored in internal registries (registry.redwood).
- Promotion: dev -> staging -> prod, with deployment artifacts immutable and traceable to a CI build id.

Threat modeling and architecture reviews:
- New public-facing services or data-sensitive changes require a lightweight architecture review (security review checklist) and a formal threat model for high-impact changes.

Developer training & attestations:
- Annual secure-coding training required for engineers; completion tracked in LMS.
- All engineers with prod access complete quarterly attestation of access and secrets hygiene.

5) Incident Response: Security Procedures

Objectives: detect, contain, eradicate, recover, and follow-up while preserving chain-of-custody for evidence.

Escalation matrix and communication:
- Severity taxonomy: sev1 (data exfiltration/customer-impact), sev2 (service degradation with potential data impact), sev3 (non-customer impacting security event).
- PagerDuty rotations: security-oncall, sre-oncall, and product-incident-lead.
- External communications: Customer-facing communications drafted by CSM + security with legal sign-off for sev1 incidents.

Investigation playbook (high-level):
1. Triage & containment: snapshot hosts, rotate affected credentials, isolate compromised machines.
2. Evidence preservation: export logs to immutable evidence store, capture network flows, and collect forensic images when warranted.
3. Scope identification: enumerate affected customers/resources via inventory service.
4. Eradicate & recover: deploy fixes through canary rollouts, validate in staging before mass rollout.
5. Post-incident review: incident report (postmortem), root-cause analysis, and action items tracked with owners and SLA.

Chain-of-custody and legal:
- Forensic exports use signed manifests and are stored in the evidence bucket with access time-limited via presigned links.
- Legal and privacy must be engaged for any extraction of customer data beyond logs.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Goal: produce auditable evidence for SOC2, ISO27001, and customer audits with minimal operational overhead.

Evidence catalog and automation:
- Evidence types: policy documents, architecture diagrams, control tests (logs, screenshots), signed attestations, penetration test reports.
- Evidence pipeline: scheduled collectors (audit-collector job) gather logs, configuration snapshots, ACL exports, and push to compliance evidence vault (WORM store).
- Mappings: each control has a mapping to audit evidence artifacts and owner; mapping stored in compliance-tracker (spreadsheet + Confluence index).

Audit lifecycle:
1. Evidence collection (automated where possible) with signed manifests.
2. Reviewer verification (security or compliance) marks evidence as "verified" in tracker.
3. Export package generation for auditors with read-only pre-signed links and a timeboxed approval.

SLA: baseline evidence for quarterly control reviews prepared within 5 business days of request.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Risk acceptance process:
- Any deviation from documented controls must be submitted as a Risk Exception Request (RER) in the risk register.
- RER fields: control-id, justification, compensating controls, owner, expiration date, mitigation plan.

Approval and monitoring:
- Low-risk exceptions are approved by security manager; mid/high-risk require cross-functional review (security director + legal + product).
- Exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days for high-risk without remediation plan) and reviewed monthly.

Compensating controls examples:
- If MFA cannot be applied to an older system, require single-purpose bastion host with jump box auditing and session recording.
- If logs cannot be retained in-region, use encrypted cross-region logs with access restricted to specific service accounts and additional approval.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Example IAM policy snippets and authz rules (inline code examples and CLI commands).
- Appendix B: Audit log storage architecture diagram (text description and S3 lifecycle table).
- Appendix C: Incident response checklist (playbook excerpt with PagerDuty runbooks).
